records.human_notes_or_page: Integrated Report p.114–115: Board “ultimately accountable” for sustainability and climate strategy under IFRS S1/S2; dedicated **Board Sustainability Committee** and **Risk Management and HSE Committee** meet at least quarterly; mandates include climate risk in ERM and monitoring sustainability targets. Remuneration architecture references sustainability/climate KPIs in the sustainability governance narrative (p.115 monitoring/KPI feedback loop; Remuneration Committee p.83).

p.114: day-to-day execution led by CEO and SLT via **Sustainability Management Committee (SMC)**; SMC meets monthly and reports to SLT and Board; functional roles across Finance, Operations, Risk, etc. (p.113–115).

p.138–150: climate risks in **physical** and **transition** categories (plus emerging litigation); Climate Risk table with impacts and mitigations; short/medium/long-term framing in sustainability metrics section (p.111 targets table).

p.149–150 and strategy sections: Niger Delta exposure (extreme weather, sea-level rise, regulatory change); integration across upstream, midstream gas and new energy value chain; asset/facility context for onshore vs offshore emissions programmes.

p.151: quantitative resilience testing using IEA **Current Policies (CPS)**, **STEPS**, and **NZE** scenarios from World Energy Outlook 2025; IEA price paths tested against the strategic business plan.
p.48–51, 114: full Group ERM integration (including offshore); Risk & HSSE Committee incorporates climate into enterprise risk framework with quarterly evaluation of mitigations.

p.9, 150: End of Routine Flaring (EORF) projects completed on operated onshore assets; zero-routine flaring on WA; EA programme progressing 2026; linked to emissions intensity reduction and capital gas projects (ANOH, Sapele).
p.108–111: Scopes **1, 2 and 3** disaggregated onshore/offshore/Group; intensity 24.3 kgCO2/boe onshore; Gross Scope 1 reduction vs 2020 baseline disclosed with ktCO2e figures.

Strong extractive operational metrics (flaring elimination %, fugitive ID to NUPRC requirements p.25, spills/HSE). IFRS/SASB alignment claimed in reporting ecosystem; full EM-EP reserve-life sensitivity not evidenced at investor-grade depth → **2**.
p.111: 2020 baseline; onshore EORF by 2026; 70% Scope 1 reduction ambition; methane 40–50% reduction by 2026; net-zero roadmap referenced in strategic priorities.

p.25: fugitive emissions identification in Western Assets “to NUPRC requirements”; methane reduction programme with quantitative tCO2e. Measurement pilots/LDAR implied; full NUPRC MRV template architecture not fully documented → **2**.
p.9–13, 150: quantitative onshore flare reduction (e.g. 37% / 86% flaring eliminated messaging); zero routine flares target 2026 onshore; gas commercialization via ANOH/Sapele.

Financial statements disclose impairment and decommissioning/abandonment (PIA fund modalities p.19; impairment lines in financial review). **No detailed quantitative reconciliation** of climate scenario assumptions into IAS 36/37 → **1**.

Clear **operated / onshore operated assets** boundary for sustainability targets (p.111); operational control statistics disclosed. Explicit dual-boundary JV/PSC sustainability reconciliation incomplete → **2**.

Robust monitoring, internal control and governance over sustainability data (p.114–115). External ISSA 5000-ready ICS for non-financial data not claimed; limited to management/Board assurance pathways → **2**.

Sustainability Report p.64 / ERM section p.48–49: Board oversight via **Risk, Environment, Social and Governance (RESG) Committee**; quarterly review of risk processes; mandate covers EHS, environmental stewardship and ESG strategy. Climate metrics tied to executive remuneration **not evidenced** → **2**.

p.48: ERM & Control Function reports through Executive Director, Corporate Services to GCEO, with RESG oversight; risk report escalated quarterly. Specific climate “champion” org chart thinner than Seplat SMC model → **2**.
p.11–12, 22: physical climate hazards (e.g. flooding) and energy-transition / policy risks identified in materiality and CEO narrative; timelines/granularity by business line only partial → **2**.

Materiality maps impacts across own operations / upstream / downstream value chain (p.11–13); flooding vulnerability of critical assets noted. Facility-by-facility stranded-asset analysis limited → **2**.
No climate scenario analysis (IEA NZE or similar) identified in the 2025 Sustainability Report or FS pack.
p.19, 48–49: climate change elevated among Group’s most significant strategic risks within the **Enterprise Risk Management Framework**; RESG quarterly oversight.
p.18–19, 43: gas infrastructure, commercialization and flare-reduction initiatives; LDAR/OGI campaigns at Brass and Kwale. Link to capital budgets/ARO incomplete → **2**.
p.43: 2025 inventory discussed; **Scope 2 not included**; Scope 1/3 managed via EHS policy and LDAR narrative. Meets “partial disclosure (Scope 1 only)” → **1**.

p.3: material metrics under **SASB Oil & Gas Exploration and Production**; flaring, venting, fugitive and spill management described (p.11, 42–43). Not full EM-EP with reserve-life sensitivity → **2**.
p.17–19: ambition of net-zero GHG by **2060** and alignment with NUPRC routine flare elimination by **2030**; measurable company baseline year / interim GHG milestones incomplete → **2**.
p.22, 43: NUPRC methane/environmental mandates acknowledged; **LDAR using OGI** at terminals/plants (measurement pilots). Full NUPRC MRV template architecture not detailed → **2**.
p.18–19: flare reduction and gas commercialization supporting NUPRC 2030 objective; zero environmental fines claimed (p.43). Asset-by-asset flaring volumes/penalties reconciliation limited → **2**.
FY2025 FS: impairment of non-financial assets and decommissioning provision are audit focus areas (auditor risks). No explicit climate-assumption crosswalk to IAS 36/37 → **1**.

Report scope covers Oando Plc and subsidiaries (p.5 area); JV/NAOC integration discussed operationally. Dual-boundary equity/operational reconciliation for sustainability metrics not explicit → **1**.
Internal Audit chapter; GRI 2-5 notes **partial external assurance of OERNL GHG data planned** for future periods (GRI index ~p.83–85). Pre-assurance posture, not ISSA 5000-ready ICS → **2**.

Annual Report ~p.61–62: Board **Sustainability Committee** membership listed; Chairman (~p.19–20) states Board strengthened sustainability embedding and voluntary IFRS S1/S2 adoption. Meeting frequency, climate metrics and rem linkage not detailed → **2**.
Executive/management sustainability roles not described with reporting lines or board update cadence beyond general governance → **1**.

p.42–45: structured **ERM** (ISO 31000 / COSO) with Internal Audit review; climate not shown as integrated into the principal risk matrix → **1**.

No Scope 1/2/3 GHG inventory or intensity metrics located.

Qualitative commitment to eliminate routine flaring / emissions reduction focus (~p.19, 27); no GHG baseline year or net-zero pathway with milestones → **1**.
NUPRC referenced in market/regulatory overview (~p.22–23), not as company measurement-based methane MRV status → **1**.
Quantitative/operational flaring elimination programme and gas monetisation narrative (~p.18–22, 37); not asset-by-asset volumes with NUPRC baseline reconciliation → **2**.
ARO write-back / decommissioning liabilities and impairments disclosed in financial review (~p.39–40). No climate-assumption reconciliation to IAS 36/37 → **1**.
